title: weekly-sync-serving-runtime-infra-console-agenda-prep-2026-04-06
content:
Weekly sync prep (personal notes / scratchpad)
Date: Tue 2026-04-06 · Meeting 30m (weekly)
Owner / note-taker: Ethan Park
Location: #eng-serving-runtime (Zoom)
Goal for this week: quick alignment on infra incidents, console rollout status, and a short decision on model routing fallback defaults. Keep it tight — mostly blockers and AIs.

Participants (expected): Jordan, Priya, Liam, Maya (ops), Sam (SRE), Ethan

Agenda (30m)
1) Quick round (3m) — one-line headlines from each subteam (runtime / infra / console) — Ethan to start
2) Incident recap: storage GC spike on 2026-04-03 (7m) — Priya leads
   - Impact summary: brief outage for 10m affecting 2 Dedicated pools (EU-west), increased p99 by 120ms for hosted API
   - Root cause hypothesis: concurrent compaction + heavy batching; unclear interplay with prefix cache eviction
   - Prep: Priya to bring current logs + timeline (linked SRV-4521)
3) Console rollout status and telemetry (6m) — Jordan
   - Are we green on rollout metrics (errors < 0.5%, latency SLO met for API routes)?
   - Watchlist: new trace view causes console front-end throttling during big org loads
   - Prep: Jordan to confirm rollout percentage and current error groups (confluence link above)
4) Model routing fallback defaults (8m) — decision item (Ethan/Jordan)
   - Proposal: change default fallback from 1 cheaper quantized variant to 2-tier fallback (same-region cheaper then cross-region identical model) to reduce p99 spiky regressions during capacity pressure
   - Tradeoffs: slightly more cost when cross-region fallback triggers, but better end-user latency stability
   - Prep: Ethan to summarize telemetry showing 3 recent spikes where single fallback caused degradations; Priya to provide capacity thresholds
5) Action items & quick sync (6m) — capture AIs, owners, and due dates

Parking lot / quick notes to self
- Bring up the KV-cache eviction tuning RFC (defer to next week if we run out of time)
- Check with Ops on autoscale cooldown setting changed 2026-03-29 (might be related to GC timing)
- Remind Jordan to add a short blurb in release notes about trace-view performance mitigations

Prep checklist (what I need before the meeting)
- Priya: timeline + logs for storage GC spike (SRV-4521) — ask for one slide or 3 bullet timeline in chat before meeting
- Jordan: rollout metrics screenshot + top 3 error groups
- Liam: brief note on fallback simulation results (if available) — otherwise we'll capture AI to run sim after meeting

Notes (to capture in meeting)
- If Priya confirms compaction overlap, immediate temporary mitigation: increase compaction window jitter and reduce concurrent compaction limit (Ops runbook steps)
- Console trace-view throttle root cause: backend paging API returning large trace lists, frontend not paginating early — mitigation: backend early-paging + front-end skeleton loader
- Decision on routing fallback: if we agree, implement feature-flagged 2-tier fallback with opt-in default rollout for 2 weeks then flip to default if no regressions

Follow-up / action-items (working list)
- AI-1: Priya Nair — compile timeline + logs for 2026-04-03 storage GC spike; share 1-slide timeline in #eng-serving-runtime before meeting; due 2026-04-06 (meeting).
- AI-2: Jordan Li — export rollout metrics (errors, p99 latency) for console rollout and post screenshot to confluence; due 2026-04-07.
- AI-3: Liam OConnor — run fallback simulation for 2-tier vs 1-tier on representative workload and share short results; due 2026-04-10.
- AI-4: Ethan Park — draft RFC for 2-tier fallback feature-flag implementation and rollout plan; due 2026-04-13.
- AI-5: Sam R. (SRE) — check autoscale cooldown change on 2026-03-29 and report any correlating capacity anomalies; due 2026-04-09.
- AI-6: Jordan Li — add release-note blurb for trace-view performance mitigation to 2026-04 release notes; due 2026-04-08.

Personal follow-up (post-meeting)
- Reconcile meeting AIs and update tracker (I will update this doc and create a shared sheet if more than 6 AIs).
- If decision made, create feature-flag story and tag product + security for Private deployment impact review.

Quick links (scratchpad)
- SRV-4521 (Jira) — storage GC spike
- Confluence: SERVING-RUNTIME-weekly — current rollout notes and metrics
- GitHub: repo/ops#123 — autoscale cooldown change PR

End of prep notes. Keep concise in meeting — prioritise incident mitigation and fallback decision.
